ghana-poultry-rice-tariffs.whole: The IMF and World Bank said in July 2004 that Ghana had reached the HIPC debt-relief completion point. They put total relief from all creditors at US$3.5 billion in nominal terms (US$2.2 billion in present value), saving about US$230 million a year in debt payments from 2004 to 2013. The same IMF release reports real GDP growth rising from 3.7% in 2000 to 5.2% in 2003, and poverty falling from 51% (1992) to 39% (2000), while a recent survey showed child and infant mortality rising. These figures come from the lenders' own release; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: IMF and World Bank Support US$3.5 Billion in Debt Service Relief for Ghana

malawi-grain-reserve.whole: The reserve cut was meant to save money: an EU-funded study recommended reducing the end-1999 stock of 167,000 tonnes to a buffer of 30,000-60,000 tonnes, because stored maize lasts only a few years and the IMF says holding it would cost the equivalent of one-fifth of Malawi's yearly health spending (IMF). The government sold nearly all of it in 2001 expecting a large harvest; the IMF's representative said it 'did not even keep the 60,000 mt that their own policy required' (The New Humanitarian). In mid-2002 inflation was 22% and interest rates 46% (The New Humanitarian). The IMF suspended its PRGF loan and its share of debt relief in 2001 over overspending, especially on state companies (IMF).

sources_add.title: IMF Civil Society Newsletter: Malawi food crisis

nigeria-fuel-subsidy-2012.whole: The government estimated that ending the subsidy would save 1 trillion naira in 2012 (The Globe and Mail). The chairman of a House of Representatives committee investigating the subsidy said ships had discharged 59 million litres of fuel a day while the country used 35 million; the committee heard that the subsidy paid on the difference came to 669 billion naira (about US$4.14 billion) a year (The Globe and Mail). This was a parliamentary committee's estimate during its inquiry, not a court finding.

sources_add.title: Nigeria investigates $4-billion fuel subsidy fraud
Jonathan cuts fuel prices, Nigeria protests suspended

zambia-textiles-collapse.whole: The World Bank's own evaluation office (OED, 2002) said Bank support helped restore modest, private-sector-led growth in the late 1990s: non-mining GDP grew about 3.2% a year, the fastest since independence, and agriculture about 4% a year. The same review found growth was not enough to raise average income: GNP per person fell from $450 in 1990 to $300 in 2000, poverty stayed above 70%, and urban poverty rose sharply. It also said the adjustment lending had financed an unsustainable debt overhang. This review is the lender's own; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Zambia Country Assistance Evaluation

cambodia-resin-trees.whole: The project was a US$5 million World Bank 'Learning and Innovation Loan' approved in 2000 to improve management of logging concessions and to monitor and prevent forest crime. By the Bank management's own account, illegal logging dropped sharply after the late 1990s and the area under concessions shrank during the project; no independent check of those figures was found. Management also agreed that the management plans prepared by the concession companies were deficient.

sources_add.title: Cambodia: Improving Management of Forests is Critical to Better Livelihoods, Economic Growth in Cambodia

ijora-oloye-lagos-1998.whole: The Lagos Drainage and Sanitation Project, approved in 1993, cost $89.1 million, with $63 million lent by the World Bank's IDA and the rest paid by Lagos State. It built about 50 km of storm drains with bridges and culverts across areas including Lagos Island, Apapa, Surulere, Yaba, Mushin and Oshodi. Bank management rated it satisfactory and said overflow into homes had been eliminated where drains were finished; these are the Bank's own ratings, and no independent check was found. Management said the project affected 286 people in all, each resettled or compensated.

sources_add.title: Management Response: Nigeria Lagos Drainage and Sanitation Project

pronaca-santo-domingo.whole: Pronaca is Ecuador's largest producer of poultry and pork (CAO). The IFC lent it US$20 million in 2004 to expand and upgrade facilities and US$30 million in 2008, and Mongabay puts IFC's total funding at US$120 million by 2013, including a loan of up to US$70 million for livestock expansion in Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas. The company has built more than 30 pig and poultry farms in the province since the 1990s; residents estimate about 1 million pigs (Mongabay). Ecuador's Environment Ministry licensed 14 of the farms in December 2014 (Mongabay). No figures on jobs or output were found.

sources_add.title: World Bank-funded factory farms dogged by alleged environmental abuses

danosha-pig-farms.whole: The ombudsman (CAO) lists a US$70.6 million IFC equity commitment from 2013 to expand Axzon's Ukrainian arm Danosha, which then ran about 10 pig farms, one biogas plant and more than 11,000 hectares of farmland in Ivano-Frankivsk region; IFC exited in 2021. The EBRD lent €35 million in 2014 for expansion, waste disposal, EU-standard animal welfare and two biogas plants expected to produce over 15,000 MWh of electricity and heat a year, by the EBRD's own projection; no independent check of output was found.

sources_add.title: Ukraine: Axzon-01/Halych and Kalush
EBRD in €35 million loan to pig farmer Danosha

bankers-patos-marinza.whole: In 2009 the IFC approved US$65.4 million (a US$55 million loan and US$10.4 million equity) toward a US$370 million plan to develop the Patos-Marinza heavy oilfield, with the EBRD also invited to lend. The IFC expected the government to receive 50% income tax and 10% royalties, and the company had about 200 staff in Albania at the end of 2008 (IFC). Bankers reported average output of 19,767 barrels a day from its Albanian oilfields in the first quarter of 2015, and royalties of about US$10 million for that quarter. Output and royalty figures come from the company's own reports; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Bankers Petroleum - Summary of Proposed Investment
Bankers Petroleum Announces 2015 First Quarter Financial and Operational Results

titan-egypt-cement.whole: The IFC committed €80 million to Titan's Egyptian cement business, whose investment programme added a second 1.5 million-tonne-a-year production line at Beni Suef; the two plants together can make 3.5 million tonnes a year (CAO). The ombudsman's 2021 investigation found IFC had helped the company gradually reduce air emissions and address dust, and noted better use of protective equipment by workers, but found monitoring was not enough to show the plants met World Bank Group standards for stack emissions, dust or noise.

sources_add.title: Egypt: Alex Dev-01/Wadi al-Qamar

montelimar-sugar-ckd.whole: The IFC lent US$15 million in 2013 toward a US$38 million expansion of the Montelimar mill, then the smallest of Nicaragua's four sugar mills. The IFC projected milling would rise from 2,300 to 4,100 tonnes of cane a day, sugar output from 33,000 to 67,000 tonnes a year, and about 1,300 new jobs; its results page lists 2022-2024 results as 'Not Available', and no independent check was found. The former workers' cooperative set up through CAO mediation runs a textile factory that employs 15 community members (CAO).

sources_add.title: Ingenio Montelimar - Summary of Investment Information

eco-oro-santurban.whole: In March 2009 the IFC agreed to buy CAD 12 million of Greystar shares (about 12.5% of the company), its first mining investment in Colombia, to fund final studies to bring Angostura to the mine-development stage; it said the mine would bring jobs and government revenue but gave no figures (IFC). Eco Oro later sued Colombia for about US$690 million; an ICSID tribunal ruled in July 2024 that it had proved no damages, and Colombia paid nothing (Vanguardia).

sources_add.title: IFC Invests in Greystar to Support Development of Angostura Gold Project
Ombudsman Finds IFC Failed to Comply with Own Investment Standards on Eco Oro Minerals in Colombia
Colombia no pagará ni un dólar a Eco Oro por demanda por explotación de oro en Santurbán

okko-revutskoho-kyiv.whole: The EBRD and IFC arranged a US$180 million syndicated loan for Galnaftogaz in 2013, with up to US$100 million more from the IFC in parallel, to open up to 60 new filling stations on a network of almost 400 and to expand storage, shops and cafés (EBRD). A further US$35 million IFC loan in 2020 paid for upgrades to OKKO stations and terminals, fast chargers for electric cars and fuel and fertiliser credit for farmers; the IFC said the company employed up to 10,000 people, up from about 2,000 at its first IFC loan. These figures come from the lenders' own releases; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: EBRD and IFC organise syndicate financing for Ukraine's Galnaftogaz
IFC Supports Ukraine's Galnaftogaz to Modernize its Infrastructure and to Benefit Farmers

gmr-kamalanga.whole: The IFC made a US$100 million equity commitment in 2007 to the India Infrastructure Fund, which invested in GMR Kamalanga Energy (CAO). Global Energy Monitor lists three 350 MW coal units (1,050 MW) running since 2013-2014, selling power to Odisha, Bihar, Haryana and other parts of India. A fourth 350 MW unit received environmental clearance in July 2025, but satellite images in June 2026 showed no construction (Global Energy Monitor).

sources_add.title: Kamalanga power station

maple-energy-ucayali.whole: The IFC approved up to US$10 million of equity in Maple Energy in July 2007 to pay for drilling and well work-overs at its two ageing oilfields near the Ucayali River, oil exploration, and a new ethanol project (CAO). The 35 million-gallon-a-year sugarcane ethanol plant had recently begun operating and had exported its first shipment by September 2012 (Biodiesel Magazine). No output figures for the Ucayali oilfields were found.

sources_add.title: Maple Energy announces financial results for first half of 2012

agrokasa-ica-aquifer.whole: The IFC lent Agrokasa US$6 million in 1999 to develop high-value horticulture, partly guaranteed a 2005 group bond, and approved US$15 million in 2006 to expand asparagus exports, build up avocado production and upgrade a farm in Barranca. By the IFC's account the company sold fresh asparagus and table grapes in 28 countries; the IFC gave no job or export figures, and no independent check was found. A further commitment of up to US$10 million was withdrawn by the company (CAO).

sources_add.title: IFC Supports Peruvian Agribusiness Expansion (Agrokasa)

wilmar-sambas-riau.whole: The IFC made four investments in the Wilmar Group from 2003; the two named in the complaint were a US$33.3 million guarantee and a US$17.5 million loan (CAO). No figures on what these investments produced were found. In Sambas, CAO-led talks produced agreements in late 2008 giving villagers access to land not yet converted to plantations and larger community investment funds (CAO). The World Bank admitted errors in its lending procedures (The Ecologist).

sources_add.title: World Bank breaks rules in lending to palm oil companies

antamina-huarmey.whole: MIGA issued six guarantees worth US$107.5 million in 1999-2000 for the Antamina mine, which sends its mineral concentrates by underground pipeline to its port at Huarmey (CAO). MIGA expected the project to employ 6,000 Peruvians during construction and operation, by its own projection; no independent check was found. Antamina produced 435,378 tonnes of copper in 2023, making it Peru's second-largest copper mine, with a US$2 billion expansion planned to extend its life to 2036 (Reuters via Mining.com).

sources_add.title: Compañía Minera Antamina S.A.
Peru's No. 2 copper mine Antamina sees production steady in 2024

karachaganak-berezovka.whole: The IFC board approved financing in 2002 for part of Lukoil's share of developing the Karachaganak oil, gas and condensate field, with a loan agreement signed in October 2002 (CAO audit). CAO's case page lists IFC loans of US$50 million, US$75 million and US$25 million, meant to raise crude oil and condensate output. No figures on the field's output or revenue to Kazakhstan were found on the pages opened. The ombudsman's audit found the monitoring IFC relied on could not show compliance: IFC's monitoring reports gave no stack data for hydrogen sulphide or volatile organic compounds, and the air sampling sites, about 3 km from the plant, were not shown to be where pollution peaks or where people live.

sources_add.title: Kazakhstan: Lukoil Overseas-02/Berezovka

interagua-guayaquil.whole: Interagua took a 30-year concession in 2001, backed by an US$18 million MIGA guarantee (CAO), with targets of 95% water and 90% sewer coverage and 55,238 free new connections of each kind in poor areas. Before the concession about 64% of residents had piped water and 46% sewers; by August 2005 Interagua had made 37,966 connections, 2% above its target for that period, and the share of customers paying their bills rose from about 50% to 84% (Grupo FARO study, 2006). The same study estimated that the poorest fifth of households became about 7% less likely to have water over the decade, that water prices rose compared with publicly run Quito, and that water losses were about 67% against Quito's 30%; its authors say the comparison cannot isolate the effect of privatisation.

sources_add.title: Ecuador: Interagua-01/Guayaquil
Stay Public or Go Private? A comparative analysis of water services between Quito and Guayaquil

mozal-bypass.whole: Mozal cost US$2.2 billion, half from equity investors and half from development-bank loans; it made up about 30% of Mozambique's official exports and used 45% of its electricity (AL Circle, republishing The Guardian, 2013). A report by Jubilee Debt Campaign, Tax Justice Network and Justiça Ambiental found the smelter paid a 1% turnover tax in place of profit tax and VAT; it estimated the government received about US$15 million a year while about US$320 million a year went to foreign investors, governments and development banks. BHP said 93% of Mozal's staff were Mozambican and the IFC cited 'tens of thousands' of direct and indirect jobs, figures with no independent check found. A 2025 report says Mozal exports about 600,000 tonnes of aluminium a year (Torre.news).

sources_add.title: Mozal smelter benefited foreign interests more than the people of Mozambique, say campaigners
Mozal Thrives, Mozambique Struggles: Aluminium Giant Confirms 27 Years of Tax Exemptions

allain-duhangan.whole: The IFC committed US$45 million in loans to the 192 MW run-of-river plant on the Allain and Duhangan tributaries of the Beas River (CAO). Statkraft, which owns 49%, says the plant began commercial operation in April 2010 and generates 802 GWh a year, a company figure with no independent check found.

sources_add.title: Allain Duhangan hydropower plant

jordan-bread-riots-1996.whole: Jordan entered IMF programmes in 1989, when output shrank almost 11% and inflation rose above 25%, after a 1988 budget deficit of 23% of GDP before grants and with external public debt at 174% of GDP; the 1996 subsidy cut came under a 1996-1999 Extended Fund Facility (IMF Independent Evaluation Office, 2005). The IMF's evaluation office rated the IMF's role 'moderately successful': it found stabilisation achieved, external viability restored and debt ratios 'fallen substantially' over 15 years, and counted replacing food subsidies with targeted cash transfers among the reforms that worked. It said fiscal sustainability was only partly achieved and that outcomes cannot be attributed to the IMF alone. This is the IMF's own evaluation office; no outside evaluation was found.

sources_add.title: Evaluation of the IMF's Role in Jordan: Summary
Evaluation of the IMF's Role in Jordan: Chapter 1

costa-rica-imf-protests-2020.whole: After the 2020 protests the government and IMF agreed a revised US$1.778 billion, 36-month loan in early 2021 that ruled out privatisations and higher taxes on consumption or pensions; it aimed to cut a deficit of 8.3% of GDP and reach a primary surplus by 2023, with central government debt at 69.7% of GDP in 2020 (Tico Times). Measures included a 0.5% tax on luxury homes and transferring up to 30% of 14 state companies' profits to the treasury. Fitch reported a 2021 primary deficit of 0.3% of GDP, 3.1 points lower than in 2020 and well under the 1.7% target agreed with the IMF, and raised Costa Rica's outlook to stable (Delfino).

sources_add.title: IMF approves $1.8 billion loan for Costa Rica
Fitch mejora perspectiva crediticia de Costa Rica tras resultados fiscales de 2021

simandou-rio-tinto.whole: After decades of delays, Simandou began production on 11 November 2025 when the first ore reached Morebaya port by rail (Caixin; The Star), and a 200,000-tonne shipment of ore left for China on 2 December (The Star). Rio Tinto and Chinese companies spent more than US$20 billion on the mines, a 650 km railway and the port, and up to 50,000 people worked on construction at its peak (The Star). The mines are expected to reach 120 million tons of ore a year, with full output targeted for mid-2028 (Caixin). Guinea's government holds a 15% stake in each mine and a similar stake in the infrastructure venture (The Star). No figures on IFC's role were found on the pages opened.

sources_add.title: First China ore shipment rewards Guinea coup leader's push for Simandou alliance
China-backed Simandou iron ore project starts production in Guinea after decades of delays

campo-maan-bagyeli.whole: FEDEC, the foundation set up in March 2001 in connection with the Chad-Cameroon pipeline, received a starting endowment of US$3.5 million from the pipeline company COTCO; it says its funding covers 680,000 hectares, about one-eighth of Cameroon's protected areas, including Campo Ma'an National Park (264,000 hectares). For Campo Ma'an it reports sustainable farming rising from 0 hectares in 2018 to 17 in 2021 and beekeeping from 0 to 23 apiaries. These are FEDEC's own figures; no independent check was found, and no figures on what the park has done for wildlife were found.

sources_add.title: FEDEC presentation (CAFE 2021)
sources_add.publisher: Fondation pour l'Environnement et le Développement au Cameroun (FEDEC), via BIOFUND

plantar-minas-gerais.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project, backed by its Prototype Carbon Fund and BioCarbon Fund since 2001, was establishing 11,600 hectares of managed tree plantations by 2012, and the UN climate body had issued it more than 4 million temporary carbon credits; the Bank gave no tonnage or payment figure, and no independent check of results was found. Carbon Trade Watch (2009) reported the Prototype Carbon Fund expected to buy over 1.5 million credits, worth about US$25 million at US$15 each. It also reported that the CDM board rejected the original forestry proposal, and that some 143 local groups and individuals called the claim that Plantar would otherwise have switched to coal 'absurd'.

sources_add.title: Finding a Sustainable Balance between Industry and Nature
Marketing the Climate

lafarge-meghalaya-shella.whole: The IFC approved a US$35 million loan, up to US$10 million in syndicated loans and US$10 million of equity in 1998, investing in 2003; it projected about 282 permanent local jobs in Bangladesh and Meghalaya, a figure with no independent check found (IFC). The US$270 million plant had started producing cement by December 2006, with initial capacity of 1.5 million tonnes a year, about 10% of Bangladesh's demand, fed by a 17 km conveyor (7 km of it in India) from the Meghalaya quarry (CemNet).

sources_add.title: Lafarge begins cement production in Bangladesh

kpone-landfill-tema.whole: The World Bank-supported engineered landfill was meant to last 15 to 25 years but ran for about 10 before it was capped in 2019, after it became the main dump for seven assemblies when the Insumia landfill closed, according to a Tema Metropolitan Assembly engineer (Ghana News Agency). Zoomlion began re-engineering and closing the site in June 2020; by May 2023 gas wells had been drilled to draw off methane, leachate pipes laid and about 35 hectares covered (Graphic Online). In February 2026 an older landfill site that the Assembly reopened as an emergency measure was taking 600-800 tonnes a day, with waste at 24 metres or more against a 16-metre design height, and frequent leachate overflows (Ghana News Agency).

sources_add.title: Sanitation time bomb looms as Kpone landfill nears capacity
Kpone landfill site re-engineering works 90 per cent complete

mai-ndombe-redd.whole: In June 2025 the World Bank paid the DRC US$19.47 million for 3.89 million tons of emission cuts in Mai-Ndombe, the first payment under an agreement worth up to US$55 million for 11 million tons; it gave no share for communities beyond saying a significant share would go to them under a benefit-sharing plan (World Bank). The tonnage is the Bank's own figure; no independent check was found. The DRC's national rules, finalised in February 2025, send 25% of REDD+ revenue to local people (The Independent, Uganda). The same report says the 300,000-hectare Mai Ndombe concession developed by Wildlife Works, operating since 2011, averts about 2.8 million tonnes of CO2 a year, a figure from the head of the Mai Ndombe REDD+ Initiative with no independent check, and that community committees spent credit-sale money on 12 renovated schools and 11 solar-powered wells.

sources_add.title: DRC: Communities set to benefit as country receives $19.47 million for reducing deforestation emissions
In Congo, carbon credits are paying out

bisri-dam.whole: The dam was meant to supply clean, continuous water to 1.6 million people in Greater Beirut and Mount Lebanon, by the World Bank's account, at a total cost of $617 million; the project took off in 2014 after Lebanon's cabinet approved it (Arab News). The World Bank committed $474 million and had paid out $230 million when it partly suspended funding on 26 June 2020 (Rivers without Boundaries). In September 2020 it cancelled the remaining $244 million, citing unfinished preconditions for construction, and the dam was never built (World Bank; Arab News).

sources_add.title: Bisri: Lebanon's dam of contention
Next Dam(n) Lesson for the World Bank: People Saved the Bisri Valley in Lebanon

chandil-subernarekha.whole: The Subernarekha Multipurpose Project was meant to irrigate land in Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal and to generate hydropower near Chandil; work took off in 1998 with a NABARD loan (Indian Express, 2012). Its estimated cost rose from Rs 5,200 crore in 2008 to Rs 5,500 crore in 2009, which officials put down to higher raw material prices (The Telegraph), and stood at Rs 6,613 crore in 2012, when nearly 60% of the work was done; that report gave no figures for irrigation or power delivered (Indian Express). In August 2025 Odisha's revenue minister said work on the Chandil Dam remained incomplete because the states had not coordinated (PTI).

sources_add.title: Decades of delay jack up Subernarekha project costs
Odisha govt seeks governor's intervention to complete dam projects in Jharkhand

qmm-fort-dauphin.whole: MIGA said the sixth generator was meant to ease power shortages in Fort Dauphin (estimated population 360,000, about 31% with electricity), with the power sold to the state utility JIRAMA under a 10-year contract; it gave no capacity or customer figures. Rio Tinto says it has invested about $1 billion in QMM over 25 years (Mining Weekly), and its own 2025 report says QMM paid $11.1 million in taxes to Madagascar in 2024, up from $7.1 million in 2023, and employs more than 2,000 people directly, over 80% hired locally (L'Express de Madagascar); these are the company's own figures and no independent check was found. Under a 2023 agreement with the government the royalty rose from 2% to 2.5% and QMM was to pay its first dividend to the state, $12 million (Mining Weekly).

sources_add.title: Rio strikes new fiscal agreement for Madagascar ilmenite JV
MINES - Rio Tinto augmente sa contribution fiscale

shwe-taung-cement-thazi.whole: IFC's disclosure says the expansion adds a 4,000-tonne-a-day kiln with a 5 MW waste-heat power unit to a plant that began operating in 2014 with a 1,500-tonne-a-day kiln; limestone use was to rise by 2 million tonnes a year and coal from the group's mine from 60,000 to 150,000 tonnes a year (via Early Warning System). The disclosure gives no figures for jobs or cement output. The Shwe Taung Group's website lists its cement capacity as 2 million tonnes a year, without saying which plant; this is the company's own figure and no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Building Materials

mangla-dam-mirpur.whole: Mangla began operating in 1967 with four 100 MW turbines (400 MW) and reached 1,000 MW of capacity in 1994; a refurbishment aims to raise it to 1,310 MW (The Energy Industry Times). By WAPDA's count the reservoir's live water storage was 5.88 million acre-feet at completion, fell to 4.6 by 2004 from silting, and was raised to 7.5 by a project begun in 2004; WAPDA gives no figures for water delivered for irrigation. These are mostly the operator's own figures; no independent check of generation or irrigation benefits was found.

sources_add.title: Mangla Dam filled to maximum; reservoir attains 1242 feet level
Mangla refurbishment project to increase generation capacity

lihir-gold-mine.whole: By Newmont's figures, Lihir produced 670,000 ounces of gold in 2023, held reserves of 17.5 million ounces at the end of that year and employed more than 5,100 people (Australian Mining Review). Newmont also says that in 2025 the mine produced 585,000 ounces, paid PNG K1.1 billion in taxes, royalties and other government payments, paid about K162 million in royalties and compensation to landowners, and bought K1.24 billion of goods and services from PNG businesses; it puts tax and government payments since 1997 at more than K6.49 billion (US$1.5 billion) (EMTV). These are the company's own figures; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Newmont Lihir contributes more than K1.1 billion to PNG
Newmont's Lihir: One of Papua New Guinea's largest gold mines

santa-cruz-lata-airfield.whole: The World Bank says its $89 million Second Solomon Islands Roads and Aviation Project (approved 2022) pays for upgrades at Honiara and Munda airports and Santa Cruz (Lata) airfield, air navigation systems in Makira-Ulawa and Temotu, four bridges in Malaita and roads in Western Province; it gave no figures for people served or jobs. In April 2025 Civil Aviation reports put the SBD$117 million Lata upgrade at 43% complete; the runway is 1,310 metres, and a planned extension waits on an agreement with landowners after a boundary survey (In-depth Solomons). No results have been reported yet.

rogun-dam.whole: The World Bank gives Rogun a planned capacity of 3,780 MW and says it needs $6.29 billion to complete; it expects the dam to give about 10 million people in Tajikistan better access to electricity, ease winter power shortages and export about 70% of its output to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan (World Bank, 2024). In August 2025 President Rahmon said the first two units had generated 9.1 billion kWh, worth $219 million, and that more than $5 billion had been spent since 2008; completion is set for the end of 2031 (Fergana News). These output and spending figures come from Tajikistan's government; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Tajik Citizens Promised Energy Independence by August 2027

borj-chakir-landfill.whole: By early 2013 the World Bank project had paid out $20.33 million of its $22 million loan, finished a fifth waste cell at the Greater Tunis landfill and fitted gas-treatment systems at 7 of 8 targeted landfills; the share of urban people served by sanitary landfills was 63% against a 63.5% target, and the Bank rated progress 'moderately satisfactory'. These project figures are the Bank's own; no independent check was found. The Djebel Chekir gas flaring project was registered with the UN's Clean Development Mechanism in 2006 forecasting about 370,000 tonnes of CO2-equivalent cut a year; the UN registry lists about 464,000 carbon credits issued in total for November 2008 to June 2016 (summed from its listing).

sources_add.title: Implementation Status & Results Report, Tunisia Sustainable Municipal Solid Waste Management Project (P095012), Sequence 11
Djebel Chekir Landfill Gas Recovery and Flaring Project - Tunisia (Project 0487)

antea-cement-kruja.whole: IFC's 2008 review describes the plant as a 3,300-tonne-a-day clinker line able to make 1.5 million tonnes of cement a year, with about 700 workers on site during construction; it estimated emissions of about 975,000 tonnes of CO2 a year and gave no permanent job count. When the plant opened in September 2010, CemNet reported it as a EUR 200 million investment able to supply the Albanian market and export. These capacity and cost figures come from the company and its lender; no independent check of output, jobs or taxes was found.

sources_add.title: Titan inaugurates new Albanian plant

bolivia-eastern-lowlands-soy.whole: During the project the value of farm output in Santa Cruz rose 96%, with soybean volumes up about fourfold and wheat about threefold, and 410 km of rural roads were improved against 300 km planned (World Bank evaluation office review, 1998). The Bank's completion report credited the project with 37% of the output increase; its own evaluation office said this share was hard to verify because the project had no detailed indicators or with/without comparison. Both rated the outcome satisfactory. These are World Bank figures; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Bolivia - Eastern Lowlands: Implementation Completion Report Review

comilog-moanda.whole: COMILOG produced about 6.8 million tonnes of manganese ore at Moanda in 2024, and Gabon was the world's second-largest manganese producer that year with about 25% of world output (US Geological Survey). Mining and quarrying made up 3.1% of Gabon's real GDP in 2023 (USGS). By the company's own accounts, reported by Gabonreview, COMILOG had 2024 revenue of 718.1 billion CFA francs, net profit of 38.7 billion, more than 2,000 direct jobs and a contribution to the national economy of nearly 600 billion CFA francs a year; no independent check of the jobs or contribution figures was found.

sources_add.title: Gabon (country minerals information)
Gabon : Comilog valide ses résultats 2024 et renforce ses investissements

ban-chaung-coal.whole: Global Energy Monitor lists the mine as starting in 2012 with a capacity of about 180,000 tonnes of coal a year (500 tonnes a day), with a 2017 proposal to double that, and reserves of about 280,000 tonnes (citing a Myanmar energy master plan). It gives no recorded figures for actual output or taxes, and its workforce figure is its own estimate. Responding to the 2017 report that linked it to the mine through its bank investments, IFC said the report had many factual inaccuracies and that many of the sub-projects named pre-dated or fell outside its investments (The Irrawaddy / Mekong Eye).

sources_add.title: Ban Chaung Coal Mine

donbas-mine-closures.whole: In 1995 Ukraine's coal industry produced 66 million tons from 276 mines with 650,000 workers, at about 100 tons of washed coal per miner a year against 400 in Poland, and cost about $1.1 billion a year in budget subsidies, cross-subsidies between mines and unpaid bills. The reform set a target of closing twenty loss-making mines a year and planned to privatize 76 profitable ones; the World Bank lent $300 million to the budget, and of the $800 million budgeted for coal in 1997, $300 million went to closures and support for laid-off workers. By 1998, 52 mines were closed or being closed, but few jobs were cut in the mines still working, and the coal ministry's $2.6 billion budget request for 1998 was denied by the Cabinet. These figures come from a 1998 World Bank note on its own programme (Lovei); no independent evaluation of the loan's results was found.

bolivia-tin-miners-1985-1986.whole: The programme's main aim was to end hyperinflation, which had reached an annual rate of about 60,000% in May-August 1985 (Morales and Sachs, NBER). Prices rose 36.8% in the first week of September 1985 and then were flat or falling in the following weeks; the authors say inflation stayed at low double-digit annual rates for the next three years, and government revenue rose from 1.3% of GNP in early 1985 to 10.3% in the rest of the year. GDP fell 2.9% in 1986, then grew by an estimated 2.3% in 1987 and 3.0% in 1988; the authors blame the downturn on outside shocks, including a 60% collapse in tin prices at the end of October 1985, which with falling gas prices and drug interdiction cost about 10% of GNP in export earnings. Jeffrey Sachs, one of the authors, was an adviser to the government that ran the programme, from late 1985 to the end of 1986 (Sachs, 2012).

sources_add.title: The Emergence of Hyperinflation, 1982-85 (Morales and Sachs), in Developing Country Debt and Economic Performance, Vol. 2
What I did in Russia

dominican-republic-1985-austerity.whole: A US audit office (GAO) report says the January 1985 decrees unified the exchange rate and raised petroleum and electricity prices, after the US had held back $50 million in aid until reforms were promised; an earlier $450 million IMF programme from 1983 had been cancelled when the government fell out of compliance. In GAO's figures real GDP grew 0.37% in 1984 and shrank 2.21% in 1985, the fiscal deficit narrowed from 7.5% of GDP in 1984 to 4.9% in 1985, and foreign debt had risen from $2.0 billion in 1980 to $3.1 billion in 1984. GAO noted that the government kept some oil subsidies because it judged that a continued rapid fall in real incomes would cause social violence.

sources_add.title: Aid Conditionality: U.S. Use of Conditions to Achieve Economic Reforms (GAO/NSIAD-86-157)

poland-nowa-huta-1988.whole: The February 1988 'Price and Income Operation' was meant to correct the most uneven prices, quietly lower real wages and improve the budget by raising taxes and cutting subsidies; economist Branko Milanovic (Soviet Studies, 1992) wrote that the government failed to achieve these aims. In his figures retail prices rose 73% by the end of 1988, but wages rose 156%, so average real wages rose about 15% (an overstatement of living standards, he notes, because shortages worsened); real food subsidies rose 56%, while the budget deficit, 2.5% of GDP in 1987, was almost eliminated through tax revenue. Prime Minister Messner's government resigned in September 1988 amid criticism of its handling of the economy and the price rises; the Deseret News report gave annual inflation as 60%, a different figure from Milanovic's 73% retail price rise.

sources_add.title: Poland's Quest for Economic Stabilisation, 1988-91: Interaction of Political Economy and Economics (Branko Milanovic, Soviet Studies 44:3)

reventazon-hydro.whole: The plant began generating in 2016 and by ICE's count produced about 10,000 GWh in its first ten years, on average about 9% of Costa Rica's yearly electricity use; ICE's president puts its construction cost at $1.4 billion (Delfino, 2026). Costa Rica's Comptroller General found the cost rose from an initial $757 million to $1,567 million, up 107%. Data from the national grid control centre (Cence) showed the plant produced 1,645 GWh in its first two years against the 3,120 GWh ICE had projected, 47% less; ICE blamed a four-month reservoir shutdown in 2018 and output from private generators (La Nación, 2018).

Planta Reventazón genera 47% menos de la energía

hidrovias-miritituba.whole: By Hidrovias do Brasil's own figures, its transfer station at Itaituba (Miritituba) can move 6.5 million tonnes of grain a year onto barges bound for its 7.2-million-tonne terminal at Barcarena; it publishes no figures on volumes actually moved, jobs or taxes, and no independent check was found. The company had 2024 revenue of R$1.35 billion, down about 30% from 2023, and a net loss of R$621.7 million (Simply Wall St). The northern ports it serves carried 37.2% of Brazil's soybean exports and 41.3% of its corn from January to October 2025 (Conab, via DatamarNews).

olam-palm-gabon.whole: In 2016 Olam planned 52,000 hectares of oil palm (45,000 at Mouila and 7,000 at Awala), aiming for about 312,000 tonnes of palm oil a year and $625 million in export earnings, roughly the size of Gabon's yearly food import bill (Oxford Business Group). Olam now says it runs four plantations, three palm oil mills and a refinery, employs more than 4,500 people and keeps 106,000 hectares, 53% of its 202,000-hectare concession, as protected forest; these are the company's own figures and no independent check was found. Olam publishes no production figures, and no reliable figure for actual output was found.

indorama-agro-uzbekistan.whole: The $285 million programme was meant to raise cotton yields from 2.5 to over 4.5 tonnes per hectare and cut water use by 30% on about 50,000 hectares, using laser land-levelling and modern ginning; these were lender and company targets, not reported results (TXF, 2021). Indorama Agro confirmed hiring 2,720 of the 13,407 permanent and seasonal workers who may have lost jobs, and farmers and staff told Dialogue Earth that yields had fallen over the previous two years. The EBRD gave the project an expected transition impact score of 57, which Dialogue Earth said was 'not even Good'. No published figures on actual yields or output were found.

kumtor-barskoon-cyanide.whole: By January 2013 Kumtor had produced more than 8.4 million ounces of gold since 1997, about 12% of Kyrgyzstan's GDP over that time and half its exports, and had added $1.9 billion to the state budget (RFE/RL). In 2011 its $941 million in sales produced $146 million in payments to the government, by economy minister Temir Sariev's count; RFE/RL described the 2009 deal that set a 14% tax on gross revenue as 'murky'. In 2017 it produced 562,749 ounces and accounted for 9.7% of GDP and 21.1% of industrial output, by preliminary figures from Kyrgyzstan's statistics committee (Times of Central Asia).

aracruz-tupinikim-eviction-2006.whole: When IFC lent in 2004, its own disclosure described Aracruz as the world's leading maker of bleached eucalyptus pulp, with 2.4 million tonnes a year of capacity, about 31% of world supply, more than 9,000 direct jobs and over $1 billion a year in revenue, mostly in foreign currency; these figures come from IFC and the company, and no independent check was found. IFC said the $50 million loan would support company-wide initiatives, including social and environmental investments, without naming them. The loan was repaid early, and no IFC report on its results was found.

bertin-maraba-cattle.whole: IFC said its $90 million loan in 2007 would support Bertin, which then had 30 plants and 30,000 direct jobs, in expanding its beef and leather business, including a tannery near the Marabá slaughterhouse, and would add 7,700 direct jobs. It said the loan would also help Bertin trace 100% of the animals and hides it processed, avoid buying cattle from protected areas or ranches without environmental permits, and fund, with Bertin, a technical assistance programme for supplying ranchers. These are IFC's own aims; no report of what was achieved before IFC withdrew in 2009 was found, and no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: Bertin Ltda: Summary of Proposed Investment (project 23792)

chenguang-kargilik-xinjiang.whole: IFC's disclosure says the loan of up to $40 million was for working capital so Chenguang, a maker of plant-based food extracts and additives that earns more than 30% of its revenue from exports, could increase production; it put the total project cost at about $30-40 million. IFC expected better product quality, training for staff and higher quality standards among Chinese food exporters, and lists the loan as completed. These are IFC's own aims; no figures on what was produced, and no independent review of results, were found.

sources_add.title: Chenguang Biotech: Summary of Investment Information (project 40616)

portucel-mozambique-plantations.whole: A 2009 agreement with Mozambique's government set a planned $2.5 billion investment, including a pulp mill to make 1.5 million tonnes of cellulose a year; by January 2025 the mill had not been built, partly because the planned deep-sea port at Macuse was delayed (Oxpeckers). The company had sent nine shipments of timber, 285,000 cubic metres in all, from Beira to Portugal, and its Zambézia nursery, opened in 2015, produced 1.3 million cloned plants a year by 2023 (Oxpeckers). How much of the $2.5 billion has been spent was not reported.

andhra-pradesh-community-forest.whole: The World Bank's evaluation office rated the first-phase project (a $77.4 million credit, closed 2000) 'highly satisfactory': about 850,000 hectares of degraded forest came under better management, more than twice the target, 2,666 village forest committees were formed, and dense forest cover in six sample districts rose about 19% from 1996. Sampled committee households gained about Rs 5,600 a year, but the studies missed losses such as less goat grazing; in the evaluators' own tribal survey 74% reported higher incomes, while everyone surveyed in villages without committees reported a fall. The same review rated the Bank's own performance unsatisfactory because forest encroachers were resettled in breach of its rules (OED, 2002). These are figures from the World Bank's own evaluation office; no independent check was found.

sources_add.title: India: Andhra Pradesh Forestry Project (Credit 2573-IN), Performance Assessment Report

sri-lanka-imf-2023-tariffs-taxes.whole: The programme aimed to raise revenue, end the crisis-era inflation and restore reserves and debt sustainability. By the World Bank's figures, Colombo inflation fell from 69.8% in September 2022 to 4% in December 2023 and below zero from September 2024; the economy grew 5% in 2024 after shrinking 9.5% over 2021-2023; usable reserves rose from 0.3 months of imports at end-2022 to 3.0 months in 2024; and public debt fell from 119.2% of GDP at end-2022 to an estimated 102.4% at end-2024. Poverty (under $3.65 a day) stood at 24.5% in 2024, twice the 2019 level, and the Bank expected over a third of people to be in or at risk of poverty in 2025. A comparison by publicfinance.lk found revenue reached 13.7% of GDP in 2024, slightly above the IMF's 13.3% forecast.

sources_add.title: Sri Lanka Development Update 2025

colombo-st-sebastian-canal-mcudp.whole: By the World Bank's own count in September 2018, the project had built or repaired 45 km of roads and drains (target met), improved 4 km of a planned 9.2 km of main canals, raised gravity drainage capacity by 110 of a planned 185 cubic metres, upgraded three public spaces and parks, turned the Beddagana wetland into a park and built 16 public toilet blocks. The Bank expected 232,000 Colombo residents to gain direct flood protection once the work was finished. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
